questions.stem: Nancy, 51, has COPD and uses home oxygen at 2 L/min. In general practice she tells you her breathlessness has been getting worse over a week. You are taking a focused history. Which question best tells you how severe this exacerbation is?
options: "How breathless do you feel right now, on a scale from 0 to 10?"
"Do you get more breathless when you lie flat at night?"
"What can you do now, and how much oxygen do you need, compared with usual?"
"Did the breathlessness come on suddenly, or over several days?"
questions.why: In COPD, measure breathlessness by what the patient can do and how much oxygen they need, compared with their own baseline. Nancy now needs oxygen almost all the time and needs it to walk from her bed to the living room.
notes: A 0 to 10 score is subjective and has no baseline, so it does not show how far she has dropped from her usual function.
Orthopnoea is a cluster question to screen for heart failure. It does not measure how severe the COPD exacerbation is.
Onset (sudden or gradual) helps tell PE or pneumothorax apart from an exacerbation, but it does not measure how severe her breathlessness is.

questions.stem: Nancy, 51, has an infective COPD exacerbation: purulent sputum, temperature 38.2 °C, WCC 13.4, CRP 62, and no consolidation on chest X-ray. She has a penicillin allergy (rash). Her GP starts treatment before transfer to ED. Which antibiotic regimen is most appropriate?
options: Doxycycline 200 mg orally first dose, then 100 mg daily, 5 days in total
Moxifloxacin 400 mg orally daily for 10 days
questions.why: In a COPD exacerbation with purulent sputum, eTG recommends amoxicillin or doxycycline for 5 days. With a penicillin allergy, use doxycycline: 200 mg for the first dose, then 100 mg daily, 5 days in total.
notes: Amoxicillin is a first-line choice for most patients, but Nancy has a penicillin allergy, so doxycycline is the better option.
Ciprofloxacin covers Streptococcus pneumoniae poorly and is not recommended for exacerbations treated in the community.
Moxifloxacin is kept for pneumonia in patients with severe penicillin allergy. It is not needed for this exacerbation, and 10 days is too long.

questions.stem: Nancy, 51, has severe COPD, an SpO2 of 88% on 2 L/min and a fever, and she is waiting for an ambulance. A colleague suggests a non-rebreather mask at 15 L/min. You explain that oxygen should be titrated to 88 to 92%. What is the main mechanism by which high-flow oxygen causes hypercapnia in COPD?
options: Removing the hypoxic drive to breathe, sensed by the central chemoreceptors
Reversing hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction, which worsens ventilation-perfusion mismatch
Raising tissue metabolic rate, so more carbon dioxide is produced
Oxygen toxicity damaging type II pneumocytes, so surfactant is lost
questions.why: High-flow oxygen reverses hypoxic vasoconstriction, so blood flows back to poorly ventilated alveoli. Dead space rises and PaCO2 goes up, with a smaller added contribution from the Haldane effect. Loss of hypoxic drive is a minor factor.
notes: Loss of hypoxic drive plays only a small part, and that drive is sensed mainly by the peripheral (carotid body) chemoreceptors, not the central ones.
Extra oxygen does not meaningfully raise the amount of carbon dioxide the tissues produce.
Oxygen toxicity takes hours to days of very high oxygen levels to develop and does not explain carbon dioxide retention.

questions.stem: Nancy's chest X-ray report says she is hyperinflated, with 8 anterior ribs visible above the right hemidiaphragm in the midclavicular line. In a normal adult on a well-inspired erect PA film, the dome of the right hemidiaphragm meets about which anterior rib?
questions.why: On a well-inspired PA film the right hemidiaphragm normally meets about the 6th anterior rib (roughly the 10th posterior rib). More than 6 or 7 anterior ribs above it, with flattened domes, suggests hyperinflation, as in Nancy's COPD.
notes: Eight anterior ribs is what Nancy's film shows, and it is a sign of hyperinflation, not a normal finding.
A diaphragm this high suggests a poor inspiration, lung volume loss or diaphragm splinting, not a normal film.
Ten anterior ribs would mean severe hyperinflation. The normal figure of about 10 counts posterior ribs, not anterior ones.
